context.question: If I should purchase Master B. his houses — shall I deal with the seller and procure money in time to pay for the purchase?
context.asked_at: 31 March 1634, 6 p.m. (figure heading as printed: '31 March 1634. 6 Hor. P.M.')
context.setting: In 1634 the inheritance of the house he lived in (in the Strand, London) and others were offered to him for sale; his own money could not be called in for six months; the seller's first demand was £530

attachments.key_positions: Sun (significator of the seller) locally placed in the 7th, received by Venus(?) in exaltation near the cusp of the 7th; lord of the 7th also lord of the 11th (Lilly's hopes); Venus applying to a trine of Saturn, lord of the 4th (the houses); Moon translating light by square aspect out of signs of long ascension; Mercury, lord of Lilly's 2nd, retrograde; Saturn lord of the 4th without material debilities except retrogradation and cadency
attachments.note: The ascending sign/degree is garbled in the 1647 OCR ('the degree of the Sign is the same wherein [Mars] was in my Radix'); positions above are those Lilly names in prose.

master_predictions.statement_excerpt: Yes — Lilly judged he should buy the houses, proceed in the matter and in the end conclude for them, though slowly and with many meetings and trouble; the seller would not abate one penny of the £530 demanded; money would be procured by borrowing (a friend would lend £500 shortly after Mercury turned direct), not from his own funds.
master_predictions.source: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II，Book II, Chap. XXXVIII 'If I should purchase Master B. his houses' (1647 pp.213–223)
key_assertions: 应买下这批房屋、推进并最终成交，但过程缓慢多波折
卖家分文不让、坚持£530
购款靠借贷（水星顺行后不久朋友借出£500）、非自有资金

outcome.description: Confirmed in detail in the text: the bargain was struck on 25 April following (the day Venus and the Sun came to their aspect); on 17 May he paid the £530 and his conveyance was sealed — 'six weeks and some days from the time of the Question'; a friend lent him £500 twelve days after (when Mercury turned direct). Lilly adds he did himself injury in money by the bargain but never repented it.

master_predictions.statement_excerpt: The report is false: 'All that we heard was untruth, and the Town neither was, or should be taken by Him or his Forces'; the news were lies, devolving to division among the enemy and no benefit to them.
master_predictions.source: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II，Book II, Chap. XXXI 'If a Report or common Rumour were True or False' (1647 pp.204–208)

attachments.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment.

master_predictions.statement_excerpt: The ship is not lost but living; she has lately been in danger (a leak or damage near her breast) but is now recovered and in harbour to repair, south-west from London on our own coasts or near those between Ireland and Wales; the sailors and officers are safe; news or certain discovery of her will come that night or within two days; and the merchant shall gain by the adventure.
master_predictions.source: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II，Book II, chapter 'Of a Ship, and her Safety or Destruction' — 'An Example of a Ship at Sea' (Fig. 4 in the 1852 edition)
key_assertions: 船未失事、仍然存活
船曾遇险（近胸部漏损）现已入港修理，位于伦敦西南方向、本国海岸或爱尔兰与威尔士之间
水手与官员平安；消息当晚或两日内到，商人将因此获利

context.question: Whether Sir William Waller or Sir Ralph Hopton should overcome?
context.asked_at: Friday 29 March 1644 (figure erected the day of the engagement)
context.setting: Friday 29 March 1644: Sir William Waller's Parliamentarian army and Sir Ralph Hopton's Royalist army were supposed engaged near Alresford, Hampshire (the Battle of Cheriton)

attachments.key_positions: Ascendant and Moon, Jupiter and Venus for Waller's side; Saturn lord of the 7th for Hopton; Moon in her exaltation with Jupiter; Sun, lord of Waller's substance/assistants, in the 10th in the very degree of his exaltation (19° Aries); only Mars and the South Node in the 9th (no supplies ready for Hopton); Saturn (Hopton's significator) sub radiis, in his fall, in no aspect to any planet, peregrine, aspecting the cusp of the 7th by square; Moon distant 11° from Venus, swift and increasing in light
attachments.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment (Fig. 20 in the 1852 edition).

master_predictions.statement_excerpt: Victory will be ours (Waller's Parliamentarian side); the enemy will be worsted, with loss and dishonour to Hopton; we shall take a considerable proportion of their ammunition though not a perfect victory without some diminution; perfect and satisfactory news will arrive within eleven or twelve hours of the question.
master_predictions.source: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II，Book II (Fig. 20 in the 1852 edition): 'A Figure erected to know whether Sir William Waller or Sir Ralph Hopton should overcome'
key_assertions: 我方（Waller一方）获胜，敌方Hopton败北受损蒙羞
将缴获相当一部分敌军弹药，但非全胜
确切消息在问卦后十一至十二小时内到达

outcome.description: Confirmed in the text: 'It appeared, by a letter from the army on that same Friday, that our generals took on the previous day 120 commanders and gentlemen, 560 common soldiers, and much ammunition.' subject.name_or_desc: A person of honour asked Lilly

context.question: If his Excellency Robert Earl of Essex should take Reading, having then surrounded it with his army?
context.asked_at: During the siege of Reading (the town was delivered 27 April; the year is printed '1644' in the 1647 OCR but the historical siege of Reading ended in April 1643 — see notes)
context.setting: Robert, Earl of Essex, Parliament's general, had surrounded Reading with his army; the town was held for the King, governor Sir Arthur Aston (spelled 'Acton' in the 1852 edition)

attachments.key_positions: Mars, lord of Scorpio (the sign ascending per the 1852 judgment), significator of Essex, well fortified except being in his fall, and in reception with the Moon (Mars in her house, she in his terms and face, near Regulus, in the 10th); Moon void of course, applying to a sextile of Mars (equivalent to a square in signs of long ascension); Sun, the King's significator, in the 7th in a fixed sign; Aquarius, the sign on the 4th, for the town; Saturn lord of the 4th for the governor, in his fall; Jupiter lord of the 5th and Venus placed therein for the town's ammunition and provision
attachments.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment (Chap. LXVI in the 1647 printing; Fig. 21 in the 1852 edition).

master_predictions.statement_excerpt: Essex shall obtain and take Reading, and gain glory and honour thereby — but with much difficulty and some fighting, and rather by composition (negotiated surrender) than by blood; the King will oppose and send relief forces with all vigour but shall not prevail; the town is strong and wants no ammunition; the way to force surrender is to set division among the principal officers against their chief; about eight days from the question they would begin to treat, and Essex would be master of the town.
master_predictions.source: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II，Book II, Chap. LXVI 'If his Excellency Robert Earl of Essex should take Reading' (1647 pp.401–405)
key_assertions: Essex将攻取Reading并因此得荣光
过程艰难有战斗，终以和约（composition）投降而非血战
约八日后开始谈判；国王救援将至但不能取胜

outcome.description: Confirmed in the text: 'The Town was delivered for the Parliament's use the 27th of April... three days after the time limited by me was expired; but the very Monday before, being eight days after the Figure set, they began to treat.' Lilly adds the King's relief was beaten back at Caversham Bridge, the Governor (Aston) was hurt in the head (as Saturn in Pisces(?) afflicted by Mars denoted), and they did not want ammunition, as Venus in the 5th signified. See the year flag in inputs (1643 historically; OCR prints 1644).

context.question: What part of the city should they search? And shall he recover the dog?
context.setting: His dog (a small beast, 6th-house signification) had strayed and was missing; London, so Lilly notes he has no example of sheep/hogs to give, only this dog

attachments.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment; several glyphs are garbled in the 1647 OCR.

master_predictions.statement_excerpt: Search west: the dog is westward from the owner's house at Temple Bar — about Long Acre or the upper part of Drury Lane, within the lines of communication (not gone out of the parish/quarter); he is indoors, in some chamber or upper room, kept privately and in great secrecy; the owner shall have his dog again, or news of him, on the Monday following or near that time.

subject.name_or_desc: A clergyman (the querent, described by Lilly as covetous, of good wit and volubility of tongue) seeking a benefice

context.question: If he should obtain the parsonage (benefice) desired?
context.setting: He had lately lost the benefit of some good place in the Commonwealth and was solicitous how to live in his former credit; he pressed his suit for the parsonage despite Lilly's advice

attachments.note: Some planet glyphs are garbled in the 1647 OCR; the seven numbered negative testimonies are Lilly's own enumeration.

master_predictions.statement_excerpt: No — the parsonage is not to be obtained; Lilly dehorted him from proceeding further. A neighbour, by letter, words or cross information, will wholly destroy his hopes; Mercurial men (scholars or divines) will be his enemies, and some woman will inform against him or prejudice him in his suit.
master_predictions.source: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II，Book II, Chap. LXXIX 'If it should obtain the Parsonage desired' (1647 pp.437–439)
key_assertions: 得不到所求教区牧师职位，不应再继续争取
一位邻居将以信件/言辞/交叉消息彻底毁掉其希望
Mercury类人士（学者/神职）将为其敌，某女子会告发或损害其申请

outcome.description: Confirmed in the text: the parson 'being covetous would proceed further... and when he thought to have the matter absolutely on his side, behold, a scurvy Letter, revealing some manifest truths concerning a Female, dashed the good Man's hopes' — he never discovered which neighbour had affronted him.

subject.name_or_desc: William Lilly himself, living in the country (Walton-on-Thames)

context.question: What became of my goods — who stole them, where are they, and can I recover them?
context.asked_at: Saturday 10 February 1637 (Old Style; 1637/8), at the moment Lilly first heard the report
context.setting: He had bought fish in London for his Lenten provision; it came by barge to Walton, and on Saturday 10 February 1637 (Old Style) a waterman told him their warehouse had been robbed the night before and his fish stolen; Lilly erected the figure for the exact time he first heard the report

attachments.key_positions: Jupiter, the only peregrine planet in an angle, on the cusp of the 7th, in Scorpio (a moist sign) — taken as significator of the thief; Mercury, significator of Lilly's goods, in Pisces (a moist sign); Part of Fortune in Cancer (a moist sign); Moon in Taurus, an earthy sign, under the earth; Mercury, lord of the 2nd, in his fall and detriment but in his own terms, applied to by sextile of the Moon (lady of the Part of Fortune) and having a trine to the Part of Fortune; Mars lord of the 7th leaving Scorpio, his own sign
attachments.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment (Fig. 19 in the 1852 edition).

master_predictions.statement_excerpt: The thief is a man whose calling is to live upon the water — a fisherman of Jupiter/Mars nature living near the Thames side, lately leaving his own house; the goods are in some low room in a moist place; there will be discovery and partial (not complete) recovery of the goods.
master_predictions.source: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II，Book II, theft chapters — 'Explanation of the above Figure' (the stolen fish), Fig. 19 in the 1852 edition
key_assertions: 窃贼是靠水为生的男子（渔夫，Jupiter/Mars性情），住泰晤士河边、近来正离旧居
货物在低矮潮湿的房间内
将有发现并部分（非全部）追回货物

outcome.description: Confirmed in the text: Lilly took out a warrant, kept it private until Sunday 18th, searched only that one house, and 'found part of my fish in water, part eaten, part not consumed; all confessed' — including seven Portugal onions the thief's wife had unknowingly made into pottage.

context.asked_at: Not stated in the text (the death Lilly timed from the figure fell on 8 October following)
context.setting: She asked Lilly about her absent husband; Lilly judged both the husband's state and, from the same figure, her own fate

妻子本人将先死：约九月底十月初（Mars对冲Saturn时）死亡或有性命大危

attachments.casting: 遇《觀》之《否》（風地觀六四動，變天地否）；所引爻辭為觀六四「觀國之光，利用賓於王」

master_predictions.statement_excerpt: 周史曰：「是謂『觀國之光，利用賓於王』。此其代陳有國乎！不在此，其在異國；非此其身，在其子孫……若在異國，必姜姓也……陳衰，此其昌乎！」
key_assertions: 所占爻辭「觀國之光，利用賓於王」主客於王庭、代有國之象
光，遠而自他有耀者；在異國、不在其身而在子孫
坤土、巽風、乾天：風為天於土上，山也；有山之材而照之以天光，故曰觀國之光
奉之以玉帛，天地之美具焉，故曰利用賓於王
風行而著於土，故知在異國；異國必姜姓，姜為大岳之後，山岳配天；陳衰則其昌
master_predictions.source: 《左傳》莊公二十二年

context.question: 衛國立嗣：立元（孫圉）還是立絷（孟絷）
context.setting: 衛孔成子夢見康叔謂已立元；孟絷足不良於行。孔成子以《周易》筮立嗣之事，以示史朝

attachments.casting_method: 蓍筮（《周易》筮占，左傳所載一爻變例）
attachments.casting: 先遇《屯》（水雷屯，靜卦），又遇《屯》之《比》（初九動變水地比）；兩卦繇皆主「利建侯」

master_predictions.statement_excerpt: 史朝曰：「元亨，又何疑焉？……康叔名之，可謂長矣。孟非人也，將不列于宗，不可謂長。且其繇曰：利建侯。嗣，吉，何建？建非嗣也。二卦皆云，子其建之。」
key_assertions: 屯卦辭元亨，二卦繇皆曰利建侯，主立侯嗣
元為康叔所名，可謂長
孟絷弱足、非完人，將不列於宗廟，不可謂長
康叔命之、二卦告之、筮襲於夢，三者相合
master_predictions.source: 《左傳》昭公七年

outcome.description: 元卒得立為嗣，是為衛靈公，享衛國、主其社稷（在位四十二年）

context.question: 断此命造（一生格局、吉凶与运程）
context.setting: 命主吴子深，江南望族，沪人所推崇之「三吴」之一；从母舅逊清御医曹沧洲学医十六七年，活人无算，画臻化境，著有《客窗随笔》；本人亦涉猎星命

attachments.pillars: 甲午 甲戌 己酉 庚午

master_predictions.statement_excerpt: 「评者议论纷纭，余独取食神，良以己土当令，又得禄于年时两午，庚金虽透，伤甲而已。日坐酉金，发越秀气，且为文昌，其艺术众长，岂偶然哉。卯运冲酉，数百万遗产，零落过半，既交辛运，食神主事，用神得助，晚景堪娱。」
master_predictions.source: 《呱呱集》韦千里·上集 https://www.luckclub.cn/pdf/bazi/017.pdf
key_assertions: 己土当令（戌月），又得禄于年、时两午，身有所依
独取食神为用：时干庚金透出、日坐酉金，发越秀气且为文昌，主艺术众长、医画双绝
庚金虽透，只伤月干甲木正官而已，不为全局之病
卯运冲日支酉金，遗产大耗；交辛运食神主事、用神得助，晚景堪娱

outcome.description: 原书自载：命主为名医兼画家（「三吴」之一），医术着手成春、画直追宋元；卯运期间数百万遗产零落过半；书成之时命主年七旬，尚力学不倦、撰《客窗随笔》（辛运晚景之断与书中叙述方向一致，属预断性质，盲测比对时以医画名家与卯运破财两项为主）
